title: WPMS/32/2024 of TAHIR HASAN Vs HDB FINANCIAL SERVICES LTD

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS

WPMS No.32 of 2024
Hon'ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
 Mr. Mohd. Alauddin, learned counsel for
the petitioner through V.C.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner/consumer
would submit that the petitioner/consumer had
taken a loan for purchase of the vehicle from the
respondent/finance company; that, due to certain
financial constraints the petitioner/consumer
committed default in payment of installments; that,
consequently the respondent/finance company
seized the vehicle of the petitioner/company; that,
being aggrieved by the illegal act of the
respondent/finance company, petitioner/consumer
preferred a complaint no.209 of 2018 (Annexure
No.1) before the District Consumer Disputes
Redressal Forum, Haridwar (hereinafter to be
referred as "Consumer Forum").
3. He would further submit that in the
Complaint No.209 of 2018 the respondent/finance
company filed an application under Order 7 Rule
11 of CPC (Annexure No.2) with averments that
there was an Arbitration Clause in the loan-cum-hypothecation agreement and as per Clause 31 of
said agreement the dispute is to be referred to the
Arbitrator under the Arbitration and Conciliation
Act 1996 and the petitioner had no occasion to file
the complaint before the Consumer Forum.
4. He would further submit that this
application of the respondent/finance company
was dismissed by the Consumer Forum vide order
dated 14.06.2022 (Annexure No.3) against which
respondent/finance company filed Revision
Petition No.19 of 2022 under Section 17 (1) (b) of
the Consumer Protection Act, 2019; that, the State
Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission,
Uttarakhand (hereinafter to be referred as
"Consumer Commission") vide order dated
07.08.23 (Annexure No.5) allowed the revision and
dismissed the complaint No.209 of 2018 of the

petitioner/consumer.
5. Learned counsel would further submit that
the order of the Consumer Commission is against
the facts and law, hence not sustainable in the eyes
of law and is, therefore, liable to be set aside.
6. Perused the record in the light of
submissions made hereinabove.
7. In the considered opinion of this Court,
admittedly there is an Arbitration Clause in the
loan-cum-hypothecation agreement. In the
impugned order, the Consumer Commission has
observed in para 9 that the arbitral award has
already been passed on 21.07.2018 and therefore
the consumer complaint which was filed by the
petitioner/consumer on 13.08.2018 was not
maintainable and could not be decided by the
Consumer Forum.
8. In the light of aforesaid, this Court does not
find any illegality or jurisdictional error in the
impugned judgment/order. No interference is,
therefore, called for. Writ petition lacks merit and
the same is hereby dismissed in limine.
